Type and number of subjects: 690 BC patient, control group 665 healthy subjects
Experimental protocol: Questionnaire about healthy lifestyle habits, including daily PA
Main findings: A positive relationship between smoking and metabolic syndrome with the risk of BC

Type and number of subjects: 972 BC patients, control group 1,098 healthy subjects
Experimental protocol: Dataset collected including lifestyle habits and serum samples
Main findings: A remarkable correlation between higher BMI, MetS, diabetes, hy-pertriglyceridemia, and tobacco consumption with BC risk

Type and number of subjects: 260 patients with prostate cancer, 438 with BC, control group of 427 people
Experimental protocol: Leisure time PA measured by the IPAQ
Main findings: PA was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer, but not with BC

Type and number of subjects: 2,341 men 86 % healthy and 14 % with cancer, diabetes or cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, or liver illnesses
Experimental protocol: Cardiorespiratory fitness measured by a 6 minutes bicycle test until exhaustion
Main findings: High cardiorespiratory fitness was associated with a significant trend for lower risk of BC and cancer of the breast or pancreas
Men with a higher BMI, more likely to be physically inactive, are more likely to develop BC

Type and number of subjects: 60 BC patients with BC, control group 60 healthy subjects
Experimental protocol: Pre-operative vigorous intensity aerobic interval exercise 3–6 weeks
Main findings: A very positive influence of the program on postoperative recovery

Type and number of subjects: 76,795 men with urological cancer, 373 with BC
Experimental protocol: Questionnaires to calculate the risk of urological cancer, including PA
Main findings: People who practice PA in free time reduce non significantly the probability of developing BC and kidney cancer

Experimental protocol: PA measured by the Godin Leisure Time Exercise Questionnaire. QL using the Bladder Utility Symptom Scale (BUSS)
Main findings: A lower weekly PA level, tobacco consumption, and a higher BMI associated with a higher recurrence or metastasis in BC

Type and number of subjects: 152,505 participants, 1,584 with NMIBC y 394 with MIBC
Experimental protocol: Analytic dataset and questionnaire data from the Janus Cohort. Leisure time PA measured by the IPAQ
Main findings: PA decreases the risk of this cancer in non-smoking men and in non-smoking and ex-smoking women
